Friction: the envelope's approval hash and revision-guard set are undocumented (implementation file read, one refused attempt), and the docs contradict each other on which envelope rules apply to in-stage writes. Separately, the recorded progress is invisible to `resume`, which still tells the learner to do the stride example she just finished (F-s04b-writes-01) — the write succeeded, but "move me on" is only half-served.

OPERATOR.md and the stage-note refusal both send the reader to WORKFLOWS §25a step 4 for the envelope, and step 4 itself says "For work inside a stage — stage-progress, stage-note, … — this section does not apply".

Which approval kind an agent should use: §8 says an agent-origin envelope claiming direct-user-gesture fails closed, and stage.progress.update is declared `admission: direct-user-gesture`; operator-approval was inferred from the envelope schema's enum, not from any sentence that says so.

internal.approval_behavior: Learner approval was scripted ("Yes, apply exactly that.") after the exact text was shown. Recorded as approval.kind operator-approval on channel operator, subject_sha256 = intent_sha256(envelope) computed with the product's own helper (tools/learning_os/contracts/gateway.py). The receipt carries intent_sha256 == approval.subject_sha256. The product checks that the approval hash matches the request; it cannot tell whether a human approved — the value is computable by whoever builds the envelope.

friction.description: WORKFLOWS §25a names `intent_sha256(envelope)` as the approval subject but no document says where the function lives, what subset of the envelope it hashes (intent_subject drops request_id and idempotency_key), or how it serializes (sorted keys, compact separators, ensure_ascii=False). Found by grepping tools/ and reading tools/learning_os/contracts/gateway.py.

OPERATOR.md (Unit workflow) and the stage-note refusal message both point to WORKFLOWS §25a step 4 for the in-stage envelope; step 4 ends with 'For work inside a stage — stage-progress, stage-note, source-feedback, detour-create — this section does not apply'.
friction.cost: 1 extra doc read and a judgment call

friction.description: The exact expected_revisions set for stage.note.write (unit only, not the study map that owns the stage) is not stated anywhere; plan-edit-context returns module, study-map and unit revisions without saying which a stage-note write needs. The refusal named the offending key precisely, so recovery was one retry.

Approval kind for an agent: stage.progress.update is declared admission direct-user-gesture and §8 says an agent-origin gesture fails closed; that operator-approval is the right kind had to be inferred from the envelope schema enum.

No product read returns a stage's working-note body: `inspect` does not resolve stages, runtime-session requires a requirement id, plan-edit-context returns only the path. The note held the most precise answer to 'where was I?' (stopped at step 4) and had to be read as a file.

After the write, resume still shows 'Evidence none recorded yet', 'Open here —' and the workspace Next-Action 'work one stride-scheduling example by hand'. The capability index has no write that advances a workspace next action, and stage-note content does not reach resume. See F-s04b-writes-01.
`resume --json` omits the 'Recorded aims' block (coordination decision and workspace next action) that the text output shows, so a machine consumer loses the sourced aims.

stage.note.write is labelled 'compatibility capability only' while OPERATOR.md routes stage-specific learning to the stage note; it is not said which capability is the current home for in-stage progress prose. stage.progress.update's payload schema types `status` as a bare string although the CLI enforces {active, paused, complete, skipped, revisit}.
Docs alternate between `python tools/los.py` and `.venv/bin/python tools/los.py`; the installation has no .venv, and the interpreter must be supplied by the consumer.
